newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Namibian bushmen object to jail extension.
newsitem.headline: Namibian bushmen object to jail extension.

text.p: Bushmen in Namibia have objected to plans to expand a jail on to land where they have set up a tourism project, a group lobbying for Bushmen rights said on Wednesday.
The South African San Institute quoted the leader of the remote Kxoe Bushman community in West Caprivi, Kipi George, as saying the government plan would destroy an important source of income.
George said his community of about 6,000 people had begun planning for the tourist camp in prime wildlife viewing territory at Ndlwavasha in 1994, with government approval.
But last week the community learned that the prisons department had decided to extend a rehabilitation centre for prisoners into the area now occupied by the camp.
The extension would also mean the Kxoe would lose some of the land, within a game reserve, which they had occupied for centuries, George said.
No comment was immediately available from the Namibian government.
